data.title: Nvidia’s 31% Surge Sparks Bursa Rebound, Tech Stocks Jump 6.17%
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia staged a strong recovery on Tuesday morning, with technology counters leading the rebound as investors regained confidence following Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, per The Star.

The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) climbed 20.02 points to 1,569.07 at 9.10am, recovering most of the losses recorded during the previous week as buying interest returned across the local market.

The rebound mirrored gains across regional markets, with South Korea’s Kospi rising nearly 6% and Japan’s Nikkei approaching a 4% gain.

Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate Huang, sending shares of the world’s largest artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker surging more than 31% overnight.

The announcement helped reverse last week’s technology-led sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% while the S&P 500 advanced 4.7%.

Apex Securities said technology stocks were particularly well positioned to extend their gains on Tuesday, supported by the global rebound and the Nasdaq’s 6.51% overnight surge.

“Technology stands out as the sector best placed to extend its gains into Tuesday, with Monday’s already-resilient +0.19% showing set to be reinforced by the overnight Nvidia-led global tech rebound and the Nasdaq’s 6.51% surge,” the research house said.

On Bursa Malaysia, the technology sector rallied 6.17%, returning to its highest level in more than a week.

MI Technovation climbed 37 sen to RM5.98, while Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) surged RM1.88 to RM37.08. Pentamaster gained 30 sen to RM4.99, SkyeChip added 17 sen to RM2.23 and ViTrox jumped 76 sen to RM9.51.

Among heavyweight counters, YTL Power International rose 29 sen to RM4.20, recovering after facing selling pressure amid concerns over its potential exposure to the Nvidia-related market turmoil.

Other blue chips also participated in the recovery, with Maybank gaining 15 sen to RM10.04, Press Metal adding 18 sen to RM6.48, Gamuda rising 12 sen to RM4.59 and Public Bank advancing 17 sen to RM8.49.

Meanwhile, newly listed Impact Capital Holdings Bhd emerged among the most actively traded counters, recording 84.05 million shares.

The Kuching-based ICT systems integrator opened at 32 sen, representing a 10 sen or 45.45% premium over its IPO price of 22 sen, before easing to 24.5 sen, still 2.5 sen above its listing price.

data.title: Ringgit Finds Little Relief As US Treasury Yields Strengthen Dollar
data.description:
The ringgit traded mostly higher against major currencies on Tuesday morning, although it remained virtually unchanged against the US dollar as expectations of further Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes continued to underpin the greenback.

At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.1205/1260 against the US dollar, compared with Monday’s closing rate of 4.1205/1250.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) was hovering around 104 points amid the Fed’s hawkish stance.

He said New York Fed President John Williams had indicated in a speech that the central bank needed to bring inflation down to its two per cent target, which he expected could be achieved sometime in 2028.

Mohd Afzanizam also noted that the two-year US Treasury yield had climbed five basis points to 4.69 per cent, with shorter-dated securities typically reflecting expectations of monetary policy changes.

“This gives the impression that there could be multiple interest rate hikes next year.

“As such, the ringgit is expected to remain under pressure against the US dollar in the near term,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened to 4.4946/5006 against the euro from 4.5214/5264 at Monday’s close, while the pound slipped to 5.3707/3778 from 5.4032/4091.

However, the local currency weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5913/5950 from 2.5896/5925 previously.

Against regional currencies, the ringgit appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1905/1955 from 3.1949/1987 but eased against the Thai baht to 12.1205/1460 from 12.1091/1274.

It was unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 226.3/226.7 and the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.46.

Bernama

data.title: Singapore Stocks Catch Wall Street’s Tech-Fuelled Wave
data.description:
Singapore shares opened sharply higher on Tuesday, tracking a strong overnight rally on Wall Street as renewed confidence in the technology sector lifted global equities.

The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) rose 73.96 points, or 1.49%, to 5,027.77 points as at 9.06am, according to Singapore Exchange (SGX) data.

Market breadth was firmly positive, with 181 advancers against 46 decliners, while trading volume reached 135.73 million securities worth S$294.05 million.

Among the STI constituents, DBS Group Holdings led the gains, climbing S$1.40, or 2.13%, to S$67.16.

Other banking heavyweights also traded higher, with OCBC Bank gaining to S$27.12 and United Overseas Bank (UOB) rising to S$35.78.

Singtel advanced to S$4.13, while Genting Singapore edged higher to S$0.53. Yangzijiang Shipbuilding also traded at S$4.35.

The positive sentiment followed a strong overnight rally on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq 100 surged 6.5% and the S&P 500 gained 4.7% on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive.

Nvidia shares soared 31% in the session, reversing some of the concerns that had weighed on global technology stocks during the previous week’s sell-off.

The development helped restore confidence in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, with investors viewing Huang’s return as a potential stabilising factor for sentiment surrounding the industry’s investment outlook.

However, gains in Singapore’s broader market were not entirely uniform.

Among real estate investment trusts (REITs), CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust slipped S$0.02, or 0.87%, to S$2.29, while other counters including CapitaLand Ascendas REIT, Suntec REIT and Frasers Centrepoint Trust traded at S$2.10, S$1.29 and S$2.11 respectively.

Elsewhere, Mapletree Industrial Trust stood at S$1.63, Frasers Logistics and Commercial Trust at S$0.82 and Mapletree Logistics Trust at S$1.04.

Despite the equity rebound, currency and bond markets reflected lingering concerns over US monetary policy, with the US dollar reaching a 19-month high and shorter-dated US Treasury yields rising as traders increased bets on a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

data.title: 22,000-Point Lifeline Fails To Sway RHB’s Bearish Hang Seng Call
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining its short position on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), despite the contract showing signs of interim support around the 22,000-point level following a recovery from its intraday low.

In its technical analysis, the research house said HSIF shed 59 points on Monday to close at 22,371 points after recovering most of its intraday losses.

The index had opened at 22,429 points, reached a high of 22,435 points and touched a low of 22,000 points before settling at 22,370 points. During the evening session, it gained 156 points to last trade at 22,527 points.

RHB Research said the long lower shadow on the daily candlestick chart suggested that interim support had emerged around 22,000 points.

However, it cautioned that the rebound did not change its overall bearish outlook, with both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving average (SMA) lines continuing to trend lower and exert downward pressure on the index.

The research house said HSIF could attempt another climb towards the 23,000-point resistance level as long as it holds above immediate support. However, a break below 22,000 points would signal a resumption of the downtrend.

RHB Research advised traders to maintain the short position initiated at 23,576 points, based on the Nov 13 closing level, with a stop-loss threshold at 23,500 points.

The first support level is placed at 21,500 points, followed by 21,000 points, while resistance is seen at 23,000 points and 23,500 points.

Despite the potential for a technical rebound, the research house said it would retain its negative trading bias on HSIF.

data.title: Stock Picks: Coraza Integrated Technology And Kelington
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Coraza Integrated Technology Bhd and Kelington Group Bhd as potential stock picks, citing bullish technical signals that could support further price gains.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said Coraza Integrated Technology could extend its upward movement after forming a bullish candlestick pattern in the previous trading session.

The stock found interim support at RM1 and recorded positive price action amid high trading volume, indicating buying interest at the level.

RHB Research said a breakout above the RM1.08 resistance would pave the way for further gains towards RM1.18, followed by RM1.27.

However, a fall below the RM1 support level would invalidate the positive outlook and potentially trigger another round of downside movement.

Meanwhile, Kelington Group could extend its technical rebound after forming a bullish reversal candlestick pattern, with a Hammer formation observed alongside high trading volume.

According to RHB Research, the pattern suggests that strong interim support has emerged, with a sustained move above the RM6.70 resistance needed to confirm the bullish setup.

A successful breakout could drive the counter towards RM7.20, followed by RM7.80.

Conversely, a decline below RM6.40 would weaken the bullish reversal signal and potentially resume the stock’s correction.

data.title: Nvidia Surge Sends S&P 500 Soaring 4.7%, Nasdaq Jumps 6.5%
data.description:
Wall Street rallied sharply on Monday after Nvidia reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, reversing last week’s global equity sell-off, while US Treasury yields and the dollar climbed amid expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Nvidia shares surged 31% after rising as much as 36% during the session, following the company’s decision to bring Huang back under pressure from US President Donald Trump.

The rally lifted semiconductor and technology stocks, with the Nasdaq 100 jumping 6.5% and the S&P 500 gaining 4.7%. Europe’s STOXX 600 also advanced 1.8%.

The rebound followed a turbulent week in which concerns over Nvidia’s leadership crisis intensified existing doubts about elevated artificial intelligence valuations and the sustainability of industry investment.

Huang’s departure had unsettled investors given Nvidia’s central role in the AI ecosystem, supplying chips to companies building AI infrastructure while also providing financing to emerging players in the sector.

“Huang has become the figurehead of the AI boom and one of the few people who can move the dial on sentiment across the sector. His departure poured petrol on an already volatile AI trade, so his return should help take some of the heat out of the market,” said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot.

Morgan Stanley Investment Management senior portfolio manager Andrew Slimmon said investors could gradually increase their exposure to technology stocks, adding that he did not believe the rebound had run its course.

Dollar And Treasury Yields Climb

In currency markets, the US dollar strengthened to a 19-month high against a basket of currencies, with the dollar index rising 0.45% to 104.31.

Shorter-dated US Treasury yields also advanced as investors adjusted their expectations for Federal Reserve monetary policy.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose around 2.37 basis points to 4.94%, while the two-year yield, which is more sensitive to interest rate expectations, climbed 7.44 basis points to 4.69%.

Gold extended its gains by 2.9% to US$3,661 an ounce, while Bitcoin rose less than 1%, paring earlier advances.

Oil prices moved in the opposite direction, with Brent crude falling 3.5% to US$89.34 a barrel as increased Middle Eastern supplies offset concerns over shipping and refinery attacks in the region.

Asian Markets Show Mixed Recovery

Asian markets delivered a mixed performance, with Taiwan’s benchmark rising 2.1% following government support measures, while South Korea’s KOSPI remained under pressure, trading 3.3% lower after recovering from a 10-month low.

The US-listed iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which provides international investors with exposure to Taiwanese equities, surged nearly 18% following news of Huang’s reinstatement.

The developments followed last week’s sharp sell-off, during which the Nasdaq Composite fell 10%, its steepest weekly decline since the pandemic-driven market rout in March 2020.

Wall Street’s Cboe Volatility Index, commonly known as the VIX or fear gauge, also climbed above 40 for the first time since April 2025.

Meanwhile, Taiwan’s financial regulator tightened short-selling rules, while Chinese stock exchanges announced measures to support equity markets, including easing requirements for margin financing.

South Korea’s finance minister reiterated the government’s readiness to stabilise the market if necessary.

Reuters

data.title: US Stocks Soar On Jensen Return, Dow Jones And S&P 500 Surge
data.description:
Stocks soared on Monday as investors cheered Nvidia’s board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. It marked a major rebound on Monday as buyers stepped back in for the holiday-shortened week after a bruising sell-off.

The S&P 500 rose 4.5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite rallied 7%.

Nvidia stock soared more than 30% Monday morning after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Nvidia’s board chair Harvey Jones said.

The move came after President Trump renewed his call to reinstate the chipmaker’s founder, Jensen Huang, as CEO amid a series of controversies.

data.title: Shanghai Index, ChiNext Closes Higher After Support Measures By Regulator
data.description:
Chinese stocks closed higher on Monday, with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index up 0.15 percent and the ChiNext Index, tracking China’s Nasdaq-style growth enterprises, gaining 3.08 percent, after a package of stock-market support measures were announced on Sunday.

The country’s securities regulator, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, announced on Sunday a cut in the minimum margin ratio for leveraged stock purchases on the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges from 100 percent to 80 percent, effective Nov. 30, a move that could theoretically inject nearly 400 billion yuan (about 59.59 billion U.S. dollars) in incremental funds.

On the same day, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, where ChiNext stocks are traded, began soliciting public opinions on the market-making rules for ChiNext-listed stocks. The rules are designed to bolster market support, strengthen market resilience, and improve the quality of market operations, according to the exchange.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed 1.93 percent higher at 10,454.37 points on Monday.

The turnover of stocks covered by the Shanghai Composite Index and Shenzhen Component Index totaled about 1.55 trillion yuan, up from 1.42 trillion yuan on the previous trading day.

Stocks related to humanoid robots and medical services led the gains, while shares in the insurance and oil and gas production sectors posted notable declines.

The STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China’s sci-tech innovation board, closed 2.62 percent higher at 1,384.58 points on Monday.

data.title: Utilities Stocks Drag Market 7.46 Points Lower
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its decline on Nov 23, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shedding 7.46 points to close at 1,549.05, as persistent selling in heavyweight utilities stocks weighed on market sentiment.

At 5pm, the FBM KLCI fell 0.48% from its close of 1,556.51 recorded on Nov 20, having traded between an intraday high of 1,555.25 and a low of 1,544.96.

Utilities counters were among the key drags, with Tenaga Nasional Bhd losing 22 sen to RM12.46, YTL Power International Bhd declining four sen to RM3.91 and YTL Corporation Bhd sliding nine sen to RM1.61.

The broader market also weakened, with the FBM 70 dropping 177.57 points, or 1.09%, to 16,102.26, while the FBM Emas declined 75.41 points, or 0.66%, to 11,416.45.

The FBM Shariah shed 110.67 points, or 0.97%, to 11,288.57, while the F4GBM slipped 5.57 points, or 0.6%, to 925.56.

Among the most actively traded stocks, Dagang NeXchange Bhd eased 1.5 sen to 40.5 sen, with 53.34 million shares changing hands, while YTL Corporation fell nine sen to RM1.61 on a volume of 50.48 million shares.

NationGate Holdings Bhd declined four sen to RM1.44, with 44.87 million shares traded, followed by CBH Engineering Holding Bhd, which lost 3.5 sen to 59 sen on a volume of 43.46 million shares.

VS Industry Bhd slipped half a sen to 24 sen, with 40.05 million shares changing hands.

Trading activity remained subdued, with total turnover declining to 3.11 billion shares worth RM2.81 billion from Nov 20’s 3.64 billion shares valued at RM2.99 billion, reflecting weaker market participation amid sustained selling pressure.

data.title: Bursa Losers Outnumber Gainers Nearly Threefold
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session on Nov 23 on a bearish note, with losers outnumbering gainers by nearly three to one, as 849 counters declined against just 293 gainers, reflecting widespread selling pressure across the market.

Market breadth remained firmly negative, with declining counters exceeding advancing stocks by 556. Meanwhile, 457 counters were unchanged, 1,242 untraded and 32 suspended.

Nestle (M) Bhd topped the losers’ list, plunging RM1.70 to RM93, followed by Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, which shed 62 sen to RM20.46, and KLCC Stapled Group, which dropped 59 sen to RM8.29.

Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd declined 38 sen to RM19.38, while Sunway Construction Group Bhd fell 37 sen to RM6.55.

Despite the broader market weakness, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd emerged as the biggest gainer, surging RM1.44 to RM35.20.

Mega Fortris Bhd advanced 23 sen to RM1.53, followed by UWC Bhd, which climbed 22 sen to RM5.65.

MISC Bhd gained 12 sen to RM7.68, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd added 10 sen to RM12.70.

Trading activity also weakened, with turnover falling to 3.11 billion shares worth RM2.81 billion compared to 3.64 billion shares valued at RM2.99 billion on Nov 20, underscoring softer market participation amid the broad-based decline.

data.title: Chinese Yuan Performance Against Ringgit And Major Currencies
data.description:
China’s currency, the renminbi or yuan, was fixed at approximately 61.36 Malaysian sen on Monday, according to the latest central parity rates released by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System (CFETS).

The official fixing placed 100 yuan at RM61.363, equivalent to RM0.61363 per yuan, while RM1 was worth approximately 1.63 yuan.

Against the US dollar, China’s central bank-linked fixing mechanism set the reference rate at 6.712 yuan per dollar.

The yuan was also fixed at 7.3496 per euro and 8.7695 per British pound, while 100 Japanese yen was equivalent to 4.2152 yuan.

Among other major regional currencies, the Singapore dollar was fixed at 5.1921 yuan, while the Australian dollar stood at 4.4426 yuan.

The central parity rates serve as official reference points for trading in China’s onshore foreign exchange market and provide an indication of the yuan’s valuation against major international and regional currencies.

Yuan Reference Rates Against Major Currencies

CFETS said the central parity rate against the US dollar was determined using a weighted average of quotations submitted by market makers before the opening of the interbank foreign exchange market.

The yuan’s reference rates against most other currencies, including the Malaysian ringgit, are calculated using average quotations submitted by participating market makers.

The fixing provides a benchmark for currency transactions involving China, Malaysia’s largest trading partner, although actual commercial exchange rates may differ depending on market conditions and financial institutions’ quoted rates.

The latest figures represent Monday’s official reference rates rather than changes in currency values, as comparative rates from the previous trading session were not provided.

data.title: Stock Today: Inari Amertron Falls 2.84% Amid Semiconductor Sector Weakness
data.description:
Shares in Inari Amertron Bhd fell 6 sen or 2.84% to RM2.05 as at 3.14pm, extending pressure on the semiconductor manufacturer.

The counter opened at RM2.06 and traded between RM2.00 and RM2.08, compared with its last traded price of RM2.11. Trading volume stood at 13.56 million shares.

The decline comes after Kenanga Investment Bank maintained its Outperform recommendation on Inari but lowered its target price to RM2.74 from RM2.77, following a 7.6% reduction in its FY2027 earnings forecast.

In a research note following the group’s first-quarter FY2027 results briefing, Kenanga lowered its FY2027 net profit forecast to RM283 million, citing weaker-than-expected profit margins. Its revised gross profit margin assumption stands at 20.7%, down from 21.5% previously.

Nevertheless, the research house said Inari’s growth outlook remained positive, supported by resilient radio frequency operations, expanding photonics production and opportunities in advanced semiconductor packaging.

Inari’s RF production utilisation remained healthy at between 75% and 80%, while its optophotonics segment recorded a 30% year-on-year revenue increase to RM140 million in the first quarter.

Kenanga also highlighted Inari Semiconductor Labs’ target to double chip-fabrication revenue to approximately RM200 million in FY2027, from RM100 million in FY2026, driven by demand for indium phosphide-based optical chips used in AI data centre connectivity.

However, raw material supply constraints and delays in specialised equipment deliveries could limit near-term growth, with stronger revenue contributions expected in the second half of FY2027.

Kenanga retained its RM2.74 target price based on a price-to-earnings multiple of 32.6 times, while identifying weak smartphone demand, supply chain disruptions and escalating global trade tensions as key risks.

data.title: Bursa Extends Losses At Midday With KLCI Down 4.79 Points
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia remained in negative territory at midday on Monday, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shedding 4.79 points or 0.31% to 1,551.72 as selling pressure continued across the broader market.

The index had touched an intraday low of 1,544.96 before recovering some ground to trade above the psychologically important 1,550-point level. It opened at 1,547.90, down 8.61 points from Friday’s close of 1,556.51.

Losses were more pronounced across the broader market, with the FBM70 falling 260.09 points or 1.60% to 16,019.74, while the FBM Emas declined 79.84 points or 0.69% to 11,412.02.

The FBM Shariah Index dropped 119.36 points or 1.05% to 11,279.88, while the FTSE Bursa Malaysia F4GBM Index slipped 5.89 points or 0.63% to 925.24.

Among the most actively traded counters, Dagang NeXchange (DNeX) fell one sen to 41 sen, with 38.27 million shares changing hands. Mega First Corporation’s warrant MAG was unchanged at 16 sen with 36.27 million shares traded, while VS Industry lost half a sen to 24 sen on 34.02 million shares.

CBH Engineering Holding declined 2.5 sen to 60 sen, with 27.73 million shares traded, while Revenue Group was unchanged at 7.5 sen after recording 24.19 million shares in volume.

Malaysian Pacific Industries was the top gainer, rising 54 sen to RM34.30, followed by Mega First Corporation’s warrant MEGAFB, which gained 18 sen to RM1.48. CEPCO added 15 sen to RM4.50, while Maybank rose 12 sen to RM9.99 and TIME dotCom gained 10 sen to RM5.55.

On the losing end, KLCC Property Holdings and Kuala Lumpur Kepong each shed 50 sen to RM8.38 and RM20.58 respectively. Fraser & Neave Holdings fell 40 sen to RM19.36, while Sunway Construction Group declined 39 sen to RM6.53 and Kelington Group lost 37 sen to RM6.46.

The midday performance came amid continued weakness across Asian markets, where technology stocks remained under pressure following last week’s sharp sell-off on Wall Street and concerns over the outlook for artificial intelligence-related investments.

data.title: Asian Markets Extend Sell-Off As Tech Stocks Face Renewed Pressure
data.description:
Asian stock markets remained under pressure on Monday as investors continued to retreat from technology shares amid concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) valuations, higher interest rates and tighter regulation, following a sharp sell-off on Wall Street.

South Korea led the regional losses, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) falling more than 4% as semiconductor heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics each shed around 4%.

The weakness followed a steep decline in US markets on Friday, when Nvidia plunged 14%, dragging the Nasdaq into negative territory for the year. The index has lost almost a fifth of its value since reaching a record high last month, despite strong earnings from Nvidia and the blockbuster initial public offering of Anthropic, the company behind Claude.

A rebound in US futures failed to restore confidence among Asian investors, with concerns over the sustainability of AI-related investments continuing to weigh on sentiment.

“These are not peripheral players in the AI boom but two of its most important semiconductor suppliers,” said SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“Their continued weakness suggests investors are still more interested in reducing exposure than celebrating a few hours of improved sentiment in US futures.”

Elsewhere, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Jakarta were also deep in negative territory, while Taiwan’s market fluctuated between gains and losses. Tokyo was closed for a public holiday.

Authorities across the region have begun considering measures to contain the market fallout. Taiwan was tightening restrictions on short-selling, while China eased access to borrowing for stock purchases. South Korea was also considering a market stabilisation fund that has not been used since the global financial crisis.

Investor anxiety was reflected in the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), commonly known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, which climbed to its highest level since April 2025.

Concerns have also intensified following the US Commerce Department’s move to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia’s advanced AI chips remotely.

Fiona Cincotta of Forex.com said “nerves have been showing in the AI trade, amid increased scrutiny over AI capital expenditure, the scale of investment, the returns on those investments and when they might materialise”.

“Furthermore, the Democrats taking control of Congress, which is expected to slow the AI buildout, combined with expectations of higher rates for longer, are fueling concerns about the sector.”

Reuters

data.title: Stock Today: Hi Mobility Edges Higher After Securing RM665.68 Million Johor Bus Contract
data.description:
Hi Mobility Berhad shares edged higher in morning trade after the company announced that it had secured a RM665.68 million contract to operate an intracity bus service network in Johor Bahru.

At 11.51am, the counter was up 0.58% or one sen to RM1.72, compared with its last traded price of RM1.71. The stock opened at RM1.72 and traded between RM1.69 and RM1.73, with 614,200 shares changing hands.

The modest gain came after Hi Mobility announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Handal Indah Sdn Bhd, had received a letter of acceptance from the Land Public Transport Agency for its appointment as the intracity bus service network operator under the Stage Bus Service Transformation programme in Johor Bahru.

The contract, valued at RM665.68 million, runs from Jan 1, 2027 to Dec 31, 2031 and covers 23 bus routes across Johor Bahru and surrounding areas.

The fleet will comprise long buses, electric buses and minibuses, serving residential communities and key destinations including Mid Valley Southkey, Toppen Shopping Centre and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia.

The services are also expected to support first- and last-mile connectivity for the upcoming Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link between Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North in Singapore.

The bus network is intended to connect residential areas with rail stations and other destinations, strengthening public transport integration across the city.

data.title: AI Infrastructure Demand Should Support Malaysia’s E&E Sector Into 1Q 2027
data.description:
CGS International expects Malaysia’s export growth to remain resilient into the first quarter of 2027, supported by sustained global demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related semiconductor products and stronger energy exports, following a sharp acceleration in trade performance in October.

In its latest economic research report, CGS said Malaysia’s exports surged 61.1% year-on-year in October 2026, the fastest growth since April 2021, driven primarily by manufactured goods.

Manufactured exports rose 68.2%, led by electrical and electronics (E&E) products, metal products, machinery, equipment and parts.

E&E exports recorded particularly strong growth of 87.2%, reflecting robust AI-related demand and increased shipments to Singapore, the United States and Taiwan.

Meanwhile, mining exports expanded 37%, supported by higher shipments of metalliferous ores, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and crude petroleum.

Agricultural exports, however, contracted 6.1%, weighed down by weaker palm oil and rubber shipments.

Malaysia’s trade surplus widened to RM41.8 billion in October, bringing the cumulative surplus for the first 10 months of 2026 to RM274.8 billion, surpassing the full-year surplus recorded in 2025.

CGS noted that imports continued to grow rapidly, increasing 54.4% year-on-year in October, compared with 52.7% in September.

Intermediate goods imports surged 64%, reflecting continued demand for manufacturing inputs, particularly those supporting E&E exports.

Capital goods imports increased 32.9%, indicating sustained investment activity, while consumption goods imports grew 11.8%.

The research house expects imports to remain elevated through the remainder of 2026 and into the first quarter of 2027, supported by continued manufacturing and export activity.

CGS expects Malaysia’s E&E sector to remain the main driver of export growth, supported by the ongoing global semiconductor upcycle and investment in AI infrastructure.

Citing World Semiconductor Trade Statistics projections, the research house noted that global semiconductor sales are expected to expand by a further 29% in 2027.

With Malaysia’s domestic E&E capacity utilisation reaching 87.7%, CGS sees limited signs of a near-term slowdown in semiconductor shipments.

The research house believes strong demand for AI infrastructure and related investments should continue supporting Malaysian E&E exports into the first quarter of 2027, despite increasingly challenging year-on-year comparisons.

Beyond electronics, CGS expects energy-related exports to contribute positively to Malaysia’s trade performance.

Higher crude oil prices and sustained regional demand have supported petroleum shipments to Indonesia, the United Arab Emirates and Pakistan, alongside increased LNG exports to South Korea.

Resilient manufacturing activity in China and ASEAN is also expected to sustain regional energy demand into early 2027.

However, CGS cautioned that weaker crude oil prices could reduce the value of Malaysia’s energy exports.

Other downside risks include a sharper-than-expected economic slowdown in the United States or China, which could weaken global technology demand, and escalating protectionist trade policies that could disrupt international supply chains.

Despite these uncertainties, CGS maintained a constructive outlook, expecting Malaysia’s exports to remain on an expansionary path into the first quarter of 2027, with AI-driven E&E demand continuing to underpin the country’s trade performance.

data.title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above US$60,000, Ethereum Rises As Crypto Market Recovers From Sell-Off
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum rebounded on Nov 23, recovering some ground following last week’s sharp cryptocurrency sell-off, although persistent market uncertainty continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, climbed 1.34% over the past 24 hours to approximately US$60,820 as of 10.15am Malaysian time, after trading between US$58,746 and US$61,648. Despite the recovery, Bitcoin remained 6.22% lower over the past seven days.

Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency, gained 1.53% to around US$1,713 as of 9.22am Malaysian time, having fluctuated between US$1,648 and US$1,733. However, it remained 5.85% lower over the preceding week.

The rebound followed a bruising week that saw Bitcoin plunge to approximately US$55,130, its weakest level since September 2024, amid widespread selling across cryptocurrencies and global financial markets.

Market sentiment remained fragile as concerns over elevated US Treasury yields, a potentially more hawkish Federal Reserve and weaker appetite for riskier assets continued to cloud the outlook.

While the latest gains offered some respite, investors remained cautious over whether the recovery could be sustained following the recent heavy losses.

data.title: Stock Today: Big Caring Holds At IPO Price In Morning Trade After Subdued Debut
data.description:
Big Caring Group Bhd shares remained unchanged at RM1.08 in morning trade, holding at their initial public offering (IPO) price following a subdued debut on Bursa Malaysia last week.

As at 10.39am, the retail pharmacy group’s shares were trading at RM1.08, with 17.46 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM1.07, touched an intraday high of RM1.09 and a low of RM1.06.

The counter’s last traded price was in line with its last adjusted closing price of RM1.08, while selling interest outweighed buying demand, with 5.36 million shares queued for sale at RM1.09 against 1.15 million shares queued to buy at RM1.08.

Big Caring made its Main Market debut on Nov 19, closing its first trading day at RM1.09, marginally above its IPO price of RM1.08.

The latest trading activity follows disclosures involving the group after its listing. On Nov 20, Big Caring revealed RM11.65 million in recurrent related-party transactions with Brego Life Sciences Sdn Bhd between Oct 1 and Nov 19, representing an aggregate percentage ratio of 2.6%.

The group said the transactions, which involved purchases and sales of nutraceuticals and medical devices as well as service-related dealings, were necessary for its daily operations and conducted on an arm’s-length basis.

Separately, filings showed that private equity investor Creador V LP’s indirect shareholding was reduced following IPO-related share disposals and an over-allotment arrangement. It retained a deemed interest of approximately 1.20 billion shares, equivalent to 16.287% of Big Caring’s issued share capital.

data.title: Gold Rebounds From 14-Month Low As Fed Rate Hike Bets Ease
data.description:
Gold prices rebounded on Monday after suffering their steepest weekly decline in eight months, with investors scaling back expectations of near-term Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

Bullion rose as much as 1.3% to around US$3,582 an ounce, recovering after a 9% slump last week that pushed prices to a 14-month low. Growing concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending also rattled global markets, triggering a sharp sell-off in technology stocks and prompting traders to reassess the outlook for US monetary policy.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that the Federal Reserve risked jeopardising the US economy by overtightening in response to the latest inflation data.

His previous attempt to rein in elevated long-term borrowing costs in August had pushed Treasury yields lower and sparked a brief rally in gold.

Swaps traders are no longer fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after Treasury yields fell across the curve on Friday. The policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield ended the session 12 basis points lower, providing support for non-yielding bullion.

Gold has fallen by around a third since the US-Iran war erupted in late February, with higher energy costs fuelling inflation and prompting central banks to raise interest rates. The metal has also traded below the US$4,000 support level since Nov 11.

Spot gold rose 1.1% to US$3,578.24 an ounce at 8.26am in Singapore, while silver gained 2.6% to US$42.21 after tumbling 15% the previous week. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dipped 0.1% after rising 0.6% last week.
